results.title: SK hynix Developing New NAND Products for KV Cache ...
results.content:
KV cache is temporary data required for graphics processing units (GPUs) to handle AI computations. As AI data surges, the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) capacity for storing KV cache is reaching its limits. In response, SK hynix plans to develop new products that mount high-capacity NAND products near the GPU, allowing them to serve as an additional KV cache repository. [...] SK hynix (000660.KS) said on the 29th during its second-quarter earnings conference call that it is developing new NAND product families such as "near-GPU storage" driven by key-value (KV) cache offloading. "We are proceeding with NAND development in a direction that most efficiently delivers the performance customers require," the company said. [...] "As the AI market expands from training to inference-centric operations, the role of NAND is rapidly changing into a key element in configuring the AI memory hierarchy," SK hynix said. "We will expand our NAND product families to secure new growth drivers."

results.title: SK Hynix and Marvell Unveil CXL Memory Module With 5.5x GPU Throughput | Gate News
results.content:
SK Hynix and Marvell unveiled CMM-Ax, a CXL-based near-memory computing module combining SK Hynix high-performance DRAM with Marvell's Structera A near-memory processing engine. The module integrates 16 Arm datacenter CPU cores into the CXL controller and delivers up to 200GB/s internal bandwidth when processing data directly within memory. The design targets large language model inference workloads, specifically KV cache operations, by processing portions of the cache in the memory domain to [...] In evaluations using 512GB configurations per device, CMM-Ax achieved 5.5 times the throughput of a single GPU and 3.6 times the throughput of dual GPUs in large language model inference KV cache processing tasks. [...] ## CMM-Ax Achieves 5.5x Throughput Gain Over Single GPU in LLM Inference Tests

The module's primary target application is KV cache processing in large language model inference. The approach processes portions of the cache within the memory domain, reducing GPU round-trip delays. In evaluations, 512GB configurations per device recorded 5.5 times the throughput of a single GPU and 3.6 times that of dual GPUs.

ITME implements differentiated fallback policies for cache misses. While a model weight miss inevitably triggers a pipeline stall, a KV cache miss is resolved through dynamic recomputation on the GPU. This design choice avoids the inefficiency of retrieving isolated missing blocks from the remote tier, which would necessitate either suboptimal chunk-sized transfers or complex retrieval logic. Consequently, recomputing the missing KV segments directly on the GPU is more performance-efficient [...] ## 6. Evaluation

### 6.1. Performance: GPU Memory (T1) vs. ITME

The performance of ITME is evaluated using the ShareGPT dataset with a configuration of 128 concurrent conversations, each spanning up to 5 turns with a minimum of 2000 tokens per conversation. As memory pressure intensifies in later stages, we focus on Turns 3–5, where the total KV cache footprint reaches 40 GB. [...] Figure 9 illustrates the time to first token (TTFT) speedup for the Llama-3.1 8B and 70B models, normalized against a GPU memory (T1) baseline utilizing recomputation. To ensure a fair evaluation, both the baselines and ITME are configured with weight offloading and prefetching enabled. To establish the upper performance bound of our architecture, we include an ideal GPU memory configuration with 80 GB, where the entire KV cache footprint resides within the local high-bandwidth memory.
